wordings.q: Your mirrors are adjusted correctly. What must you still do before you turn or change lanes?
wordings.a: Turn your head and check your blind spots
o: Look only in the inside mirror
Look only in the side mirrors
Tap the horn to warn any drivers who are beside you
wordings.why: Even properly adjusted mirrors cannot remove all blind spots. Always turn your head and check.

wordings.q: When stopping at a curb to park, how close should you get?
wordings.a: Within 18 inches of the curb
o: Within 36 inches of the curb
Within 6 feet of the curb
Within 30 inches of the curb
wordings.why: Move to within 18 inches of the curb for proper parking.

wordings.q: How far should your chest be from the air bag module, according to NHTSA?
wordings.a: 10 to 12 inches
o: 4 to 6 inches
15 to 18 inches
20 to 24 inches
wordings.why: Sit as far as possible from the steering wheel. NHTSA recommends 10 to 12 inches between the chest and the air bag.

wordings.q: A blue sign points to a rest area. What kind of sign is it?
wordings.a: A motorist services sign
o: A warning sign
A regulatory sign
A recreation and cultural interest sign
wordings.why: Blue is the background for motorist services, including police services and rest areas.

wordings.q: You see a flashing arrow panel showing a lane is closed. When should you merge?
wordings.a: Well before you reach the sign
o: Right when you reach the sign
After you pass the sign
Only when cones block your lane
wordings.why: Flashing arrow panels warn you that a lane is closed. Begin to merge into the open lane well before you reach it.

wordings.q: Two vehicles stop at an all-way stop at the same time. Who goes first?
wordings.a: The driver on the right
o: The driver on the left
The larger vehicle
The driver going straight
wordings.why: If two or more vehicles stop at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

wordings.q: You see a sign with a yellow background. What kind of sign is it?
wordings.a: A general warning sign
o: A construction and maintenance sign
A guide sign that gives directions
A motorist services sign
wordings.why: Yellow is the background color for warning signs, except construction and maintenance signs, which are orange. It is also used for school signs.

wordings.q: You see an orange sign ahead. What does the orange color tell you?
wordings.a: Construction and maintenance warning
o: A school zone with children crossing is ahead
Motorist services are nearby
A recreation area is nearby
wordings.why: Orange is used only for construction and maintenance signs.

wordings.q: Signs with a green background give you what kind of information?
wordings.a: Guidance (directions)
o: Construction and maintenance warnings
Motorist services and information
School zone warnings
wordings.why: Green is the background color for guide signs, which give directions, and for mileposts.

wordings.q: You see a fluorescent yellow-green sign. Where are you most likely to be?
wordings.a: In a school zone or pedestrian area
o: In a construction or maintenance work zone
Near a rest area
Near a hospital
wordings.why: Fluorescent yellow-green signs mark school zones and pedestrian areas, such as crosswalks. Watch for children, people on foot, and bicyclists.

wordings.q: A red, eight-sided sign is partly covered by snow, so you cannot read it. What must you do?
wordings.a: Come to a complete stop
o: Slow down and yield
Slow down for a railroad crossing
Keep going if no one is coming
wordings.why: Even when a stop sign is damaged or covered, its eight-sided shape and red color tell you to stop.

wordings.q: You come to an intersection with a sign shaped like a triangle pointing down. What does the sign tell you to do?
wordings.a: Slow down and yield to traffic
o: Always come to a complete stop
Speed up to get ahead of traffic
Stop only if a train is coming
wordings.why: A triangle pointing down is a yield sign. Slow down and yield. If no cars are coming, you do not have to stop completely. If traffic is heavy, always stop.

wordings.q: A round sign is posted beside the road. What does it warn you about?
wordings.a: A railroad crossing is ahead
o: A school crossing is ahead
A sharp curve in the road is ahead
A stop sign is ahead
wordings.why: A round sign always means you are coming to a railroad crossing. Slow down and be ready to stop.

wordings.q: Signs shaped like a diamond warn you about what?
wordings.a: A hazardous or unexpected condition ahead
o: A law you must obey, like a speed limit
Gas, food, and other services nearby
A place where you must stop
wordings.why: Diamond-shaped signs warn you about a hazard or something unexpected ahead. Be careful and usually slow down.

wordings.q: A speed limit sign is a regulatory sign. What shape is it?
wordings.a: Rectangle
o: Diamond
Circle
Octagon
wordings.why: Regulatory signs, which tell you about laws, speed limits, and lane use, are always rectangles.

wordings.q: Two lanes going your way are divided by a broken white line. May you move into the other lane?
wordings.a: Yes, you may cross it to change lanes or pass if it is safe
o: No, you may never cross a broken white line
Only to make a left turn
Only when a police officer waves you over
wordings.why: Broken white lines between lanes mean you may cross them to change lanes or pass, when it is safe.

wordings.q: The center of the road has two solid yellow lines. A slow truck is ahead, and no cars are coming the other way. May you pass it?
wordings.a: No, you may not cross the lines from either direction
o: Yes, because you can see that no cars are coming the other way
Yes, if you honk first
Yes, if the truck driver waves you on
wordings.why: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction, even when no oncoming traffic is in sight.

wordings.q: You want to pass a slow car. In the center of the road, the broken yellow line is on your side and the solid yellow line is on the other side. What does this mean?
wordings.a: You may pass when it is safe
o: You may never pass on a road with yellow lines
You may pass only on the right shoulder
You must wait for a broken white line
wordings.why: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you are in a passing zone and may pass when it is safe. When the solid line is on your side, you may not pass.

wordings.q: A traffic light is blinking yellow. What should you do?
wordings.a: Slow down and go through with caution
o: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is clear
Speed up before it turns red
Stop and wait until it turns green
wordings.why: A flashing yellow light means slow down and go ahead with caution.

wordings.q: The traffic light ahead of you changes from green to yellow. What should you do?
wordings.a: Slow down and stop, unless you are too close to stop safely
o: Speed up to beat the red light
Keep going at the same speed
Stop right away, even if you are already in the middle of the intersection
wordings.why: Yellow means the light is about to turn red. Stop if you can do so safely. Do not speed up to beat the light.

wordings.q: You are in a left-turn lane, and the signal shows a green arrow pointing left. What does the arrow mean?
wordings.a: You may turn that way, and you have the right-of-way
o: You must yield to all oncoming traffic, then turn
You may go straight or turn
You must stop first, then turn
wordings.why: A green arrow gives you the right-of-way to go in the direction of the arrow. Still yield to cars and people already in the intersection.

wordings.q: You are waiting to turn left on a green arrow. It changes to a steady yellow arrow. What does that mean?
wordings.a: Your protected turn is ending, so get ready to yield
o: You still have the right-of-way, so turn quickly
Oncoming cars must now stop for you
You may turn left only after a full stop
wordings.why: When the arrow turns yellow, your protected turn is ending. Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

wordings.q: The left-turn signal shows a flashing yellow arrow. What may you do?
wordings.a: Turn left after yielding to oncoming cars and pedestrians
o: Turn left right away, because oncoming cars must stop
Nothing, because left turns are not allowed
Turn left only after the arrow turns red
wordings.why: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left after you yield to all oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait for a safe gap.

wordings.q: Your lane has a red turn arrow. The cars in the lane next to you have a green light. May you make your turn?
wordings.a: No, all turns are prohibited
o: Yes, if no cars are coming
Yes, if you signal first
Yes, if the car behind you honks
wordings.why: When the arrow for your lane is red, all turns are prohibited, even if other lanes have green.

wordings.q: The traffic lights at an intersection are completely dark because the power is out. What should you do?
wordings.a: Treat it as an all-way stop
o: Treat it as a yield sign
Go through if you are on the bigger road
Treat it like a flashing yellow light
wordings.why: Tennessee law says a traffic signal that is not working is treated as an all-way stop. Stop as you would at stop signs.

wordings.q: Your high beams are on. You must dim them when an oncoming vehicle is within how many feet?
wordings.a: 500 feet
o: 200 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
wordings.why: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet, about one city block.

wordings.q: Your high beams are on and you are following another vehicle. You must dim them when you are within how many feet of it?
wordings.a: 500 feet
o: 100 feet
250 feet
1,000 feet
wordings.why: Dim high beams when following within 500 feet. The glare in the other driver's mirror can blind them.

wordings.q: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?
wordings.a: Stop completely, as at a stop sign
o: Slow down and go through with caution
Stop only if other cars are coming
Treat it the same as a green light
wordings.why: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, just like a stop sign.

wordings.q: Is it legal to drive into an intersection and block it after the light changes?
wordings.a: No, it is always illegal, even if there is no sign
o: Yes, if traffic is heavy and moving slowly
No, but only where a sign says so
Yes, as long as you entered before the light changed
wordings.why: It is always illegal to block an intersection, whether or not a "Do Not Block" sign is posted.

wordings.q: Your light turns green, but a vehicle is still in the intersection. What should you do?
wordings.a: Yield to the vehicle in the intersection
o: Go ahead, because you have a green light
Honk your horn to make the vehicle hurry
Go around the vehicle on the right side
wordings.why: Yield to any vehicles already in the intersection, even if you have the green light.

wordings.q: You are turning left on a regular green light (not a green arrow). Who must you yield to?
wordings.a: Oncoming cars going straight or turning right
o: Nobody, because you have a green light
Only pedestrians in the crosswalk
Only oncoming vehicles that are also turning left
wordings.why: When turning left, yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right, unless you have a protected green arrow.

wordings.q: What color are center lines on two-way streets?
wordings.a: Yellow
o: White
Blue
Red
wordings.why: Center lines on two-way streets are yellow. On one-way streets, they are white.

wordings.q: What color are center lines on one-way streets?
wordings.a: White
o: Yellow
Orange
Blue
wordings.why: One-way street lines are white. Two-way street center lines are yellow.

wordings.q: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, which lane do you turn into?
wordings.a: The first lane right of the yellow line
o: The lane closest to the right curb
The lane to the left of the yellow line
Any lane, as long as it is clear
wordings.why: Turn sharply into the first lane right of the yellow line. Move to the right lane only after signaling and checking traffic.

wordings.q: You notice the yellow line is on your RIGHT side. What does this mean?
wordings.a: You are on the wrong side, so pull over right away
o: You are in the passing lane of a highway
You are on a one-way street and are going the right way
You are in a turn lane and must turn left
wordings.why: If the yellow line is on your right, you are driving on the wrong side. Pull over immediately.

wordings.q: You miss your exit on the interstate. What should you do?
wordings.a: Go on to the next exit
o: Back up on the shoulder
Stop and wait for a gap
Make a U-turn at a crossover
wordings.why: Do NOT back up. It is illegal to back up on the interstate.

wordings.q: What is the closest you may park to a fire hydrant?
wordings.a: 15 feet away
o: 5 feet away
10 feet away
30 feet away
wordings.why: You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

wordings.q: What is the closest you may park to a crosswalk?
wordings.a: 20 feet away
o: 5 feet away
10 feet away
50 feet away
wordings.why: You may not park in a crosswalk or within 20 feet of one.

wordings.q: What is the closest you may park to a stop sign?
wordings.a: 30 feet away
o: 10 feet away
15 feet away
50 feet away
wordings.why: You may not park within 30 feet of a traffic signal, a stop sign, or any other traffic control device.

wordings.q: What is the closest you may park to a railroad crossing?
wordings.a: 50 feet away
o: 15 feet away
20 feet away
100 feet away
wordings.why: You may not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

wordings.q: You park facing downhill next to a curb. How should you set your front wheels?
wordings.a: Toward the curb
o: Away from the curb
Straight, lined up with the car
Toward the middle of the street
wordings.why: Facing downhill next to a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake. If the car rolls, the curb stops it.

wordings.q: You park facing uphill next to a curb. How should you set your front wheels?
wordings.a: Away from the curb
o: Toward the curb
Straight, lined up with the car
Toward the edge of the road
wordings.why: Facing uphill next to a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb. If the car rolls back, the back of the front wheel stops against the curb.

wordings.q: You park on a hill beside a road that has no curb. Which way should you point your front wheels?
wordings.a: Toward the edge of the road
o: Toward the middle of the road
Straight, lined up with the car
Away from the edge of the road
wordings.why: With no curb, uphill or downhill, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road, so the car rolls away from traffic if it moves.

wordings.q: You plan to turn right at the next corner. When should your turn signal be on?
wordings.a: At least 50 feet before the turn
o: Only once you start to turn
Only after you stop at the corner
Never, because right turns need no signal
wordings.why: Turn on your turn signal at least 50 feet before you turn.

wordings.q: What is the highest speed Tennessee law allows on an interstate highway?
wordings.a: 70 mph
o: 60 mph
65 mph
75 mph
wordings.why: The highest speed Tennessee law allows on interstate highways is 70 mph. Some stretches have a lower posted limit, and you should go that fast only in good conditions.

wordings.q: You are on a primary state highway, and no speed limit is posted. What is the speed limit?
wordings.a: 55 mph
o: 45 mph
65 mph
70 mph
wordings.why: Unless another speed is posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 mph.

wordings.q: On a state highway with a moderate speed limit, at what speeds does the two-second following rule work?
wordings.a: At any speed
o: Only below 30 mph
Only below 45 mph
Only above 55 mph
wordings.why: The two-second rule holds at any speed on state and U.S. highways with moderate speed limits. In bad weather, at night, and at higher interstate speeds, leave at least four seconds.

wordings.q: What do flashing yellow lights on the front and back of a school bus tell you?
wordings.a: The bus is about to stop, so slow down and get ready to stop
o: The bus is moving, so it is safe to pass it
Children are crossing the road right now
The bus is about to turn left
wordings.why: Flashing yellow lights mean the bus is getting ready to stop to load or unload children. Slow down and be ready to stop.

wordings.q: You have stopped for a school bus that has red flashing lights and its stop arm out. When may you drive on?
wordings.a: When the red lights stop, the stop arm goes in, and the bus starts moving
o: As soon as the last child reaches the sidewalk
When the bus driver honks the horn twice
After you count to 30 and see no children
wordings.why: Wait until the red lights turn off, the stop arm goes back in, and the bus starts moving.

wordings.q: You are at an intersection where a school bus has stopped to let children off. Which drivers must stop?
wordings.a: Drivers from all directions
o: Only drivers behind the bus
Only drivers coming toward the bus
Only drivers who are about to turn
wordings.why: When a school bus stops at an intersection to load or unload children, drivers from all directions must stop until the bus moves again.

wordings.q: A school bus with red lights flashing is stopped on the other side of a divided highway. A median that cars cannot drive on is between you and the bus. What must you do?
wordings.a: You don't have to stop, but drive carefully
o: Stop until the bus starts moving again
Stop, then pass slowly once the stop arm goes in
Honk your horn and keep going at the same speed
wordings.why: On a highway divided by a median or barrier that cars cannot drive on, drivers on the other side do not have to stop, but they should drive with caution.

wordings.q: You turn right onto a street that has two lanes going your way. Which lane should you turn into?
wordings.a: The lane closest to the right curb
o: The lane closest to the center line
Whichever lane has less traffic
The lane farthest to the left
wordings.why: Make a right turn into the travel lane closest to the right curb.

wordings.q: You are on a one-way street and want to turn left. Which lane should you be in before you turn?
wordings.a: The lane nearest the left curb
o: The lane nearest the right curb
The middle lane
Any lane, as long as you signal
wordings.why: To turn left from a one-way street, make your approach in the lane nearest the left curb.

wordings.q: You and two other cars stop at an all-way stop at different times. Which car goes first?
wordings.a: The vehicle that got there first
o: The largest vehicle
The vehicle going straight through the intersection
The vehicle on the left
wordings.why: At an all-way stop, every vehicle stops, and the vehicle that reaches the intersection first goes first.

wordings.q: You hear a siren, and an ambulance is coming up behind you. What must you do?
wordings.a: Pull to the right edge and stop
o: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Stop where you are in your lane
Pull to the left edge and keep driving
wordings.why: Yield to the ambulance: pull as close as you can to the right edge or curb and stop until it has passed.

wordings.q: You are halfway through an intersection when a fire truck with its siren on comes toward it. What should you do?
wordings.a: Drive on through, then pull over
o: Stop right where you are
Back up out of the intersection
Turn right at once, even if you were going straight
wordings.why: If you are in an intersection, drive on through it before you pull over, so you do not block the emergency vehicle.

wordings.q: You are on a highway with two lanes going your way. A police car is stopped on the right shoulder of your side, with its lights flashing. What must you do?
wordings.a: Move over a lane away from it, or slow down if you can't
o: Stop behind it and wait until it drives away from the shoulder
Keep going at the same speed
Flash your high beams and pass quickly
wordings.why: Move into a lane that is not next to the stopped emergency vehicle, or slow down and drive with caution.

wordings.q: On the interstate in normal conditions, what is the least following distance you should keep behind the vehicle ahead?
wordings.a: 2 seconds
o: 1 second
4 seconds
6 seconds
wordings.why: Stay at least 2 seconds behind. Increase it to at least 4 seconds in bad weather, at night, and on higher speed rural sections.

wordings.q: In bad weather, at night, or on higher-speed rural sections of the interstate, what is the least following distance you should keep?
wordings.a: 4 seconds
o: 2 seconds
3 seconds
6 seconds
wordings.why: The normal minimum is 2 seconds. In these harder conditions, use at least 4 seconds.

wordings.q: How should you use antilock brakes (ABS) in an emergency stop?
wordings.a: Apply constant, firm pressure to the pedal
o: Pump the brake pedal quickly
Tap the pedal lightly over and over
Press, release, and press the pedal again slowly
wordings.why: Push the pedal all the way to the floor if needed, even on wet or icy roads.

wordings.q: For a driver 21 or older, what is the lowest blood alcohol concentration (BAC) at which driving is always illegal in Tennessee?
wordings.a: 0.08 percent
o: 0.02 percent
0.10 percent
0.15 percent
wordings.why: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent is always illegal. You can still be charged with DUI below 0.08 if you are impaired.

wordings.q: What is the lowest blood alcohol concentration (BAC) at which an 18-year-old driver can be convicted of underage driving while impaired?
wordings.a: 0.02 percent
o: 0.05 percent
0.08 percent
0.10 percent
wordings.why: A driver who is at least 16 but not yet 21 can be convicted of underage driving while impaired with a BAC of 0.02 percent or more.

wordings.q: When you cross or enter an intersection, what must you be sure of before you go?
wordings.a: That you can get all the way across without blocking it
o: That the car behind you has stopped completely
That you can make it halfway and wait in the middle lane
That your headlights are on low beam
wordings.why: Do not block intersections. Make sure you have a big enough gap to get all the way across before you enter.

wordings.q: Your car has anti-lock brakes (ABS) and you need to stop quickly. What should you do?
wordings.a: Press the brake as hard as you can and keep pressing
o: Pump the brake pedal quickly on and off
Press the brake gently, and let up as soon as the pedal starts to vibrate
Use the parking brake instead of the brake pedal
wordings.why: With ABS, press the brake as hard as you can and keep pressing. You may feel the pedal push back. Do NOT let up.

wordings.q: You are braking hard in a car with ABS, and you feel the brake pedal pushing back. What should you do?
wordings.a: Keep the brake pedal pushed down firmly
o: Let up on the brake pedal right away
Pump the brake pedal faster
Shift into neutral and let up on the brake
wordings.why: Pushing back means the ABS is working. Do NOT let up. ABS only works with the pedal pushed down firmly.

wordings.q: Where is it best to place your hands on the steering wheel?
wordings.a: At about the 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions
o: At about the 12 o'clock position with one hand
At about the 6 o'clock position with both hands
At about the 11 o'clock and 1 o'clock positions
wordings.why: Hands at about 9 and 3 o'clock help you turn quickly and keep your wrists and forearms out of the air bag's path.

wordings.q: In a car with ABS, should you pump the brakes in an emergency?
wordings.a: No, never pump the brakes in a car with ABS
o: Yes, pump the brakes quickly to avoid skidding
Yes, pump the brakes if the pedal starts to pulsate
Yes, but only on wet or icy roads
wordings.why: Never pump ABS brakes, even if the pedal pulsates. The ABS is already pumping the brakes for you, much faster.

wordings.q: When you pass a bicyclist going the same direction, how much space does Tennessee law require?
wordings.a: At least 3 feet
o: At least 1 foot
At least 2 feet
At least 10 feet
wordings.why: Pass slowly and leave at least 3 feet between you and the bicycle. Keep that space until you are safely past.

wordings.q: Which lane must slower traffic use?
wordings.a: The right-hand lane
o: The left-hand lane
The center turn lane
Any lane they choose
wordings.why: Slower traffic must drive in the right-hand lane. The left lane is for passing and turning.

wordings.q: The crossing gates are down at a railroad crossing. When may you cross?
wordings.a: Only after the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing
o: As soon as the train passes, even if the gates are still down
Whenever you can safely drive around the gates
When the gates start to go up, even if the lights are still flashing
wordings.why: Never drive around a lowered gate. It is against the law. Wait until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing.

wordings.q: At a railroad crossing with signal devices, where must you stop?
wordings.a: Within 50 feet but no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail
o: Within 100 feet but no closer than 50 feet from the nearest rail
Within 10 feet but no closer than 5 feet from the nearest rail
Right at the edge of the nearest rail
wordings.why: At crossings with electric or mechanical signals, stop within 50 feet, and no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail.

wordings.q: You are driving near a large truck. Where are its blind spots, where the driver cannot see you?
wordings.a: Right in front, on both sides, and up to 200 feet behind
o: Only directly behind the truck, up to 10 feet
Only next to the driver's door
Only far ahead of the truck, more than 500 feet in front of it
wordings.why: A truck's blind spots, or No-Zones, are right in front of it, on both sides, and up to 200 feet behind it.

wordings.q: Children getting off a school bus should stay how far away from the bus?
wordings.a: Ten feet
o: Two feet
Five feet
Three feet
wordings.why: The area all around a school bus is the Danger Zone. Children should stay ten feet away and never go behind the bus.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a green rectangle, a red eight-sided sign, and a yellow diamond. Which sign means you must come to a complete stop? Tap the sign.

then.say: The red eight-sided sign means you must come to a complete stop. No other sign has eight sides, and this sign is always red. The green rectangle gives directions, and the yellow diamond warns of a hazard ahead.

steps.rule: The octagon is the only eight-sided sign, it is always red, and it means you must come to a complete stop.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a red eight-sided sign, a blue rectangle, and a red and white three-sided sign pointing down. Which sign means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first? Tap the sign.

targets.label: the red and white three-sided sign pointing down

then.say: The red and white three-sided sign pointing down, the yield sign, means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first. When no car is coming you do not have to stop, and when traffic is heavy you always stop. The red eight-sided sign means you must always stop, and the blue rectangle points to services for drivers.

steps.rule: A yield sign means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first, you need not come to a complete stop when no cars are coming, and you always stop when traffic is heavy.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a yellow circle, a yellow diamond, and a green rectangle. Which sign means a railroad crossing is ahead? Tap the sign.

then.say: The yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead, so you slow down and get ready to stop for a train. A round sign always means a railroad crossing. The yellow diamond warns of other hazards ahead, and the green rectangle gives directions.

steps.rule: A round sign always means you are coming to a railroad crossing, so you slow down and get ready to stop.

steps.prompt: The red eight-sided sign means you stop. The red and white three-sided sign pointing down means you let the traffic on the other road go first. The yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead. What tells you what each sign means, even from too far away to read it?
options: Its shape and its color tell you.
The words written on it tell you.
Where it stands beside the road tells you.
steps.answer: Its shape and its color tell you.

then.say: Every sign's shape and color tell you its purpose, so you know what it means before you can read it. Even when snow or dirt covers a stop sign, its eight sides and its red color tell you to stop.

steps.prompt: Four signs stand beside the road: a red eight-sided sign, a green rectangle, a yellow diamond, and a blue rectangle. Which sign means a hazard or something unexpected is ahead, such as a sharp curve? Tap the sign.

then.say: The yellow diamond means a hazard or something unexpected is ahead. A diamond sign calls for care and usually a slower speed. The red eight-sided sign means stop, the green rectangle gives directions, and the blue rectangle points to services for drivers.

steps.rule: A diamond sign means a hazardous or unexpected condition is ahead, and it calls for caution and usually a slower speed.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a yellow diamond, a white rectangle, and a yellow circle. Which sign means a law you must obey, such as a speed limit? Tap the sign.

then.say: The white rectangle means a law you must obey, such as a speed limit or which lane to use. A sign that tells you a speed limit or which lane to use is always a rectangle. The yellow diamond warns of a hazard ahead, and the yellow circle means a railroad crossing is ahead.

steps.rule: A regulatory sign, which tells you about laws such as speed limits and lane use, is always a rectangle.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a green rectangle, a blue rectangle, and a red and white three-sided sign pointing down. Which sign means directions to towns and highways? Tap the sign.

targets.label: the red and white three-sided sign pointing down

then.say: The green rectangle gives directions to towns and highways, such as which exit to take and how far it is to a town. Green is the color for signs that guide you, and for the mileposts along the highway. The blue rectangle points to services for drivers, and the red and white three-sided sign means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first.

steps.rule: Green is used for guide signs, which give directions, and for mileposts.

steps.prompt: Four signs stand beside the road: a white rectangle, an orange diamond, a yellow diamond, and a red eight-sided sign. Which sign means road work is ahead? Tap the sign.

then.say: The orange diamond means road work is ahead, so you slow down and watch for workers and their machines. Orange is used for road work and for nothing else. The yellow diamond warns of other hazards, the white rectangle states a law, and the red eight-sided sign means stop.

steps.rule: Orange is used only for construction and maintenance signs.

steps.prompt: Three signs stand beside the road: a green rectangle, an orange diamond, and a fluorescent yellow-green diamond. Which sign means a school zone or a crosswalk is ahead? Tap the sign.

then.say: The fluorescent yellow-green diamond means a school zone or a crosswalk is ahead, so you watch for children and people on foot. This bright color stands out in low light, fog and rain. The orange diamond means road work, and the green rectangle gives directions.

steps.rule: Fluorescent yellow-green is the color for school zones and pedestrian areas such as crosswalks.

steps.prompt: Four signs stand beside the road: a fluorescent yellow-green diamond, an orange diamond, a red and white three-sided sign pointing down, and a blue rectangle. Which sign means a rest area or other services for drivers are ahead? Tap the sign.

targets.label: the red and white three-sided sign pointing down

then.say: The blue rectangle means a rest area, police help or another service for drivers is ahead, because blue is the color for services for drivers. The orange diamond means road work, and the fluorescent yellow-green diamond means a school zone or a crosswalk. The red and white three-sided sign means you slow down and let the traffic on the other road go first.

steps.rule: Blue is used for motorist services, including police services and rest areas.

steps.prompt: A sign is yellow. What does its color tell you?
options: It warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve.
It warns you that road work is ahead.
It gives you directions, such as which exit to take.
It tells you that a rest area is ahead.
steps.answer: It warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve.

then.say: A yellow sign warns you of something ahead, such as a sharp curve, so you slow down and drive with care. Yellow is also used for school signs, and fluorescent yellow-green is now used for school zones too. Road work is orange, directions are green, and services such as rest areas are blue.

steps.rule: Yellow is the background for warning signs, except where orange is used, and for school signs.

steps.prompt: Every question in this lesson came down to one thing. What was it?
options: A sign's shape and color tell you what it means.
A sign's words tell you what it means.
A sign's place beside the road tells you what it means.
steps.answer: A sign's shape and color tell you what it means.

then.say: The shape and the color of a sign tell you its purpose, even from far away. That is how you know what a sign tells you to do before you can read it, and even when snow or dirt covers it.

steps.prompt: You are coming up to a steady yellow light. You can still stop safely before the intersection. You want to drive straight across. What do you do?
options: You slow down and stop before the intersection.
You speed up to get through before the light turns red.
You keep going at the same speed.
steps.answer: You slow down and stop before the intersection.

then.say: You slow down and stop before the intersection. A steady yellow light means the light is about to turn red. If you were too close to stop safely, you would go on through the intersection, but you never speed up to get through before it turns red.

steps.rule: A steady yellow light means the light is about to turn red, so you slow down and stop, unless you are too close to stop safely.

steps.prompt: You have reached a flashing red light and want to drive straight across. No other car is in sight. What do you do?
options: You come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go when it is safe.
You slow down and go through without stopping.
You stop and wait until the light turns green.
steps.answer: You come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go when it is safe.

then.say: You come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go when it is safe. A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You stop every time, even when no other car is in sight, and you do not wait for a green light.

steps.rule: A flashing red light means you come to a complete stop, the same as at a stop sign, then look both ways and go when it is safe.

steps.prompt: You are coming up to a flashing yellow light and want to drive straight across. No other car is in sight. What do you do?
options: You slow down and drive through with care.
You come to a complete stop, the same as at a stop sign.
You speed up to get through the intersection.
steps.answer: You slow down and drive through with care.

then.say: You slow down and drive through with care. A flashing yellow light tells you to slow down and take care, but not to stop. A flashing red light is the one that means the same as a stop sign.

steps.rule: A flashing yellow light means you slow down and drive through the intersection with care.

steps.prompt: When the light flashed red, you stopped and went when it was safe. When it flashed yellow, you slowed down and went through with care. What does a flashing light tell you?
options: A flashing red light means stop, the same as a stop sign, and a flashing yellow light means slow down and take care.
A flashing light means the same as a steady light of that color.
A flashing light means you may go through without slowing down.
steps.answer: A flashing red light means stop, the same as a stop sign, and a flashing yellow light means slow down and take care.

then.say: A flashing red light means stop, the same as a stop sign, and a flashing yellow light means slow down and take care. A flashing yellow light is not about to turn red, so you slow down but do not stop. A steady yellow light is about to turn red, so you stop when you safely can.

steps.prompt: The arrow over your lane is a steady green left arrow, and you want to turn left. The light over the lane beside you, for cars going straight, is a red light. On the other side of the intersection, a car facing you is stopped. Who goes first? Tap the car.

then.say: Your car goes first. The green arrow lets you turn left now, and the car facing you waits until you have turned. You still wait for any car or person already in the intersection.

steps.rule: A green arrow means you may turn only in the arrow's direction and the other traffic waits for you, after any vehicles and people already in the intersection have cleared it.

steps.prompt: You want to turn left. The green arrow over your lane has just changed to a steady yellow arrow. The light over the lane beside you is a red light. You can still stop safely before the intersection. On the other side of the intersection, a car facing you is stopped. What do you do?
options: You slow down and stop before the intersection.
You go on and turn now.
You speed up to turn before the arrow turns red.
steps.answer: You slow down and stop before the intersection.

then.say: You slow down and stop before the intersection. A yellow arrow means your turn is ending and the cars coming toward you will soon get to go, so you get ready to let them go first. You never speed up to turn before the arrow turns red.

steps.rule: A yellow arrow means your protected turn is ending, so you get ready to let the oncoming traffic go first.

steps.prompt: The arrow over your lane is a flashing yellow left arrow, and you want to turn left. The light over the lane beside you, for cars going straight, is a green light. A car coming toward you is going straight across, and it is close. Who goes first? Tap the car.

then.say: The car coming toward you goes first. A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left only after the cars coming toward you have passed and any person crossing the road has crossed. You wait for a safe gap, then turn.

steps.rule: A flashing yellow arrow means you may turn left after you yield to all oncoming traffic and to bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalk, when there is a safe gap.

steps.prompt: You want to turn left. The arrow over your left-turn lane is a steady red arrow. The light over the lane beside you, for cars going straight, is a green light. No car and no person is in the intersection or coming toward it. May you turn left now?
options: Yes
No

then.say: No, you stop and wait until the arrow over your lane lets you turn. A red arrow means you may not turn, even when the other lanes have a green light and nothing is coming.

steps.rule: When the arrow is red or your lane has the red light, every turn is prohibited, even when other lanes have a green light and the path looks clear.

steps.prompt: You are driving on a road with two lanes. The line down the middle of the road is solid yellow. What does the yellow line tell you?
options: The cars on the other side of the line are coming toward you.
The cars on the other side of the line are going the same way as you.
steps.answer: The cars on the other side of the line are coming toward you.

then.say: The cars on the other side of the line are coming toward you. A yellow line down the middle of a road separates traffic going in opposite directions.

steps.rule: Lines that separate traffic moving in opposite directions are yellow.

steps.prompt: You are driving on a road with two lanes. The line between your lane and the lane next to you is white and broken. What does the white line tell you?
options: The cars in the lane next to you are going the same way as you.
The cars in the lane next to you are coming toward you.
You may never cross the line.
steps.answer: The cars in the lane next to you are going the same way as you.

then.say: The cars in the lane next to you are going the same way as you. White lines separate lanes of traffic going the same way. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes when it is safe.

steps.rule: White lane markings separate lanes of traffic going in the same direction.

steps.prompt: The center of this road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line. The broken line is on your side. A slow car is ahead of you in your lane, and no car is coming toward you. May you pass it?
options: Yes
No

then.say: Yes, you may pass when it is safe. The broken yellow line on your side means you are in the passing zone. You must be back on your side of the road before the passing zone ends.

steps.rule: Where the center has a solid and a broken yellow line, you may pass when the broken line is on your side and it is safe.

steps.prompt: The center of this road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line. The solid line is on your side. A slow car is ahead of you in your lane, and no car is coming toward you. May you pass it?
options: Yes
No

then.say: No, you stay behind the slow car. The solid yellow line on your side means you may not pass here, even when no car is coming toward you.

steps.rule: Where the center has a solid and a broken yellow line, you may not pass when the solid line is on your side.

steps.prompt: Every question in this lesson came down to one thing. What was it?
options: What the light or the line showed told you what to do.
A sign beside the road told you what to do.
How fast the other cars were going told you what to do.
steps.answer: What the light or the line showed told you what to do.

then.say: What the light or the line showed told you what to do. Red stops you, yellow tells you to take care or that a change is coming, and green lets you go when it is safe. A yellow line has cars coming toward you beyond it, a white line has cars going your way, and you pass only when the line on your side is broken.

steps.prompt: You are driving out of a driveway and want to turn right onto the main road. There is no sign at the end of the driveway. A car on the main road is coming from your left and is close to the driveway. Who goes first? Tap the car.

targets.label: the car on the main road

then.say: The car on the main road goes first. You are driving onto the main road from a driveway, so you wait and let the car pass.

steps.rule: When you enter a main road from a driveway, an alley, a parking lot or the roadside, you yield to all vehicles already on the main road.

steps.prompt: Your road ends at a main road. There is no stop sign and no yield sign. You want to turn left onto the main road. A car on the main road is coming from your right and is close. Who goes first? Tap the car.

targets.label: the car coming from your right

then.say: The car on the main road goes first. Your road ends at the main road, so you wait for the traffic from both directions on it, even when no sign tells you to.

steps.rule: At a T intersection, the vehicles on the road that ends yield to the traffic from both directions on the main road.

steps.prompt: When you drove out of the driveway onto the main road, and when your road ended at the main road with no sign, who waited each time?
options: You did, because you were entering a road that other cars were already on.
The cars on the main road did, because they slowed down to let you in.
No one did, because the faster car went first.
steps.answer: You did, because you were entering a road that other cars were already on.

then.say: Each time, you were driving onto a main road, so you waited and let the traffic already on it go first. The law does not give anyone the right-of-way. It only says who must wait.

steps.prompt: The light ahead of you has just turned green, and you want to drive straight across. A car from your left entered the intersection before the light turned green, and it is still in the intersection. Who goes first? Tap the car.

then.say: The car in the intersection goes first. It was there before the light turned green, so you wait until it is out of the intersection before you go.

steps.rule: When the light turns green, you still yield to pedestrians and vehicles that are still in the intersection.

steps.prompt: You are coming up to a steady green light, not a green arrow, and you want to turn left. A car on the other side of the intersection is coming toward you. It is going straight across, and it is close. Who goes first? Tap the car.

then.say: The car coming toward you goes first. The green light lets you go, but your left turn crosses its path, so you wait and let it pass.

steps.rule: When you turn left on a green light that is not an arrow, you yield to oncoming vehicles.

steps.prompt: This is an all-way stop. Every corner has a stop sign with an ALL WAY sign under it. The car on your left stopped at the intersection before you got there. You both want to drive straight across. Who goes first? Tap the car.

then.say: The car on your left goes first. It stopped at the intersection before you did, so you stay stopped until it has gone across.

steps.rule: At an all-way stop, every vehicle stops, and the vehicle that reached the intersection first goes first.

steps.prompt: This is an all-way stop. Every corner has a stop sign with an ALL WAY sign under it. You and the car on your right stop at the same time. You both want to drive straight across. Who goes first? Tap the car.

then.say: The car on your right goes first. You both stopped at the same time, and when that happens the car on the right goes first. You go after it.

steps.rule: When two vehicles reach an all-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right goes first.

steps.prompt: The traffic light at this intersection is not working. It is dark and shows no color, and there is no stop sign. The car on your left stopped at the intersection before you got there. You both want to drive straight across. Who goes first? Tap the car.

then.say: The car on your left goes first. A traffic light that is not working makes the intersection an all-way stop. Every car stops, and the car that stopped first goes first.

steps.rule: When a traffic signal is not working, you treat the intersection as an all-way stop.

steps.prompt: This street has no traffic light and no sign. A person is standing at the side of the road on your right, at one end of the crosswalk, about to walk across. Who goes first? Tap the person or your car.

then.say: The person goes first. When a person is in a crosswalk or about to walk into it, you stop before the crosswalk and wait until the person has crossed.

steps.rule: You yield to pedestrians who are in a crosswalk or the street, or about to enter it, whether or not the crosswalk is marked.

steps.prompt: A person carrying a white cane with a red tip is crossing the street ahead of you, where there is no crosswalk. Must you stop and let the person cross?
options: Yes
No

then.say: Yes, you stop and wait until the person has crossed. You always stop for a person who carries a white cane, even where there is no crosswalk.

steps.rule: You always yield to a blind pedestrian who carries a white cane, including a white cane with a red tip, or who uses a guide dog.

steps.prompt: You are coming up to a green light and want to drive straight across. Two cars are stopped in your lane just past the intersection, and there is no room for your car behind them. May you drive into the intersection now?
options: Yes
No

then.say: No, you stop before you enter the intersection and wait until there is room for your car past it. You enter only when you can get all the way across without stopping. A car stopped in the intersection blocks other traffic, even when its light is green.

steps.rule: You may enter an intersection only when you can get all the way through it without stopping.

steps.prompt: Every question in this lesson came down to one thing. What was it?
options: Who must wait?
Who is driving the faster car?
Which road is the bigger road?

then.say: Every right-of-way rule tells you who must wait. When that is you, you let the other driver or the person on foot go first.
